query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing SLM process parameters by reducing hatch spacing and fine-tuning laser power and scan speed will improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity, while decreasing defects such as lack-of-fusion porosities in additively manufactured CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy components relative to conventional settings.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy components produced by laser powder bed fusion that exhibit dimensional inaccuracies and mechanical inconsistencies due to suboptimal process parameters.
generation.intervention: Adjust the SLM process by decreasing the hatch spacing combined with tailored laser power and scanning speed adjustments to achieve uniform remelting and optimal melt pool overlap.
generation.conditions: Processing conducted via selective laser melting under standard laboratory AM conditions for CoCrFeMnNi alloys, using parameter ranges that allow full melt pool overlap and controlled remelting (guided by single-track printability maps).
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced melt pool geometry resulting in improved interlayer bonding and reduced porosity, leading to a more homogeneous microstructure.
generation.mechanism: Reduced hatch spacing increases the overlap between sequential melt tracks, while optimized laser power and scan speed promote controlled remelting that homogenizes the microstructure and minimizes defects such as lack-of-fusion pores and local compositional inhomogeneity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Components manufactured with the optimized parameters will exhibit tighter dimensional tolerances, higher tensile strength and ductility, and a lower incidence of fabrication-induced defects compared to those produced with conventional parameter settings.
generation.baseline: Components produced using conventional SLM process parameters, including larger hatch spacing and non-optimized combinations of laser power and scanning speed, which typically result in noticeable porosity and dimensional deviations.
generation.boundary: The improvement is anticipated under established SLM conditions for CoCrFeMnNi alloys; however, the benefits may vary for different alloy compositions or with extreme parameter settings that could induce new defect modes such as keyholing.
generation.uncertainty: The specific magnitude of improvement in mechanical properties and defect reduction is uncertain and will depend on precise process calibration and machine-specific factors.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two groups of CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy components using SLM: one group with conventional process parameters and another group with the optimized parameter set (reduced hatch spacing, tailored laser power and scanning speed). Use identical geometries and maintain all other conditions constant.
measurements: Dimensional tolerance assessment using coordinate measuring machine (CMM)
Microstructural analysis via scanning electron microscopy (SEM) for porosity evaluation
Mechanical testing including tensile strength and ductility measurements
Density measurements using the Archimedes method
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the components processed with the optimized parameters do not show a statistically significant improvement in dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and a reduced defect density compared to the baseline group, then the hypothesis is falsified.

To achieve this, we devise two distinct LPBF processing strategies denoted as “H” and “L” (detailed in “Methods”) to produce SS316L with high and low thermal stability, respectively. During LPBF, a thin layer of metal powders is spread over a build platform and then selectively melted by a high-power laser source (Fig. 1a). Melting occurs sequentially as the laser is scanned back and forth in tracks that fill the areas to be consolidated. The H and L strategies differ in how close melt tracks are to one another within a single layer (i.e., the melt track area density), which is determined by the hatch spacing parameter, h. They also differ in how many times the same layer is scanned by the laser; namely whether the previously consolidated material is remelted or not. Medium entropy alloy (MEA) is a hot spot in the field of material research in recent years. At present, the most widely used processing method of MEAs is “casting-rolling-heat treatment”, and the preparation of CoCrNi MEA by laser additive manufacturing (LAM) is still in primary stage. In this study, CoCrNi MEAs were fabricated with different scanning speeds by laser additive manufacturing, and the influence of scanning speed on its mechanical properties was investigated. The results show that higher scanning speed can significantly improve the mechanical properties of CoCrNi MEA. Compared with the low-speed laser additive manufacturing (LSLAM) MEA, the tensile strength of high-speed laser additive manufacturing (HSLAM) MEA is increased by 5.6 % and the fracture strain is increased by 60 %, which is mainly due to the entanglement of 1/6<112> and 1/2<110> dislocations and the defect structure at the grain boundary. LAM is a promising technology that can promote the development and application of MEAs in industry.

Figure 4 depicts the surface morphology of 16 groups of single passes of the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy laser cladding orthogonal experiment. It can be observed that the macroscopic quality of the cladding is satisfactory, the surface roughness is minimal, and there are no discernible defects such as cracks, folds, and so forth. The cross-sectional morphology is depicted in Figure 5, demonstrating that the fusion cladding layer renders a strong metallurgical link with the substrate, and no defects such as cracks and peeling are observed. The orthogonal experimental scheme and cross-sectional measurement results are shown in Table 4. From the data in Table 4, it can be seen that during the laser cladding process of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, the mechanism by which process parameters affect the cladding effect is very complex, and no obvious change law can be found from the data alone.

Analogous phenomena and patterns have been identified by other scholars in their investigation of the GS-Fe01 iron-based alloy powder laser cladding process []. In conclusion, in the actual AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy laser melting and cladding production and application, it is of paramount importance to prioritize the control of the powder feeding rate if the objective is to achieve a higher microhardness, to prioritize the control of the laser power if the objective is to achieve a lower dilution rate, and to prioritize the control of the scanning speed if the objective is to achieve larger aspect ratio.

chosen.approach: AM process parameter optimization via laser power, speed, and hatch spacing
